So, there was this one city in Iraq that was particularly bad. The unit there had to abandon their FOB in the city, so there were no American forces in the city for two weeks.

We're staged a little ways outside the city, and we're told PSYOPS has been air dropping pamphlets saying that we were going to retake the city, and telling civilians to evacuate. Then we get the call, stand down. We drive a few hours back to the city where our FOB was.

The next day, we're going back to the city, mission is back on, but we're taking a completely different route. Dark of the night, driving a 32 ton vehicle over pontoon bridges and shit, scary how those things rock.

Zero-dark-thirty, already tired, took us a few hours to get there, and we're poised just outside the city. Waiting. If there's one thing I learned in the Army, it's how to wait, just staring through the VVS-2 driver's night vision. The VVS-2 was such garbage, like first generation night vision(I just looked it up, it's from 1973, perfect for warfare in the 21st century....). Two Brigade Combat Teams, waiting.

BREAK BREAK BREAK

Net call goes out to proceed into the city, and "anyone on the streets is to be considered hostile".

We roll in guns blazing. Through my fish bowl night vision I could see the whole city light up with rounds going into it. Four dudes run to get into a car, fuck you, they're dead too.

No one was attacking us...

We move to a phase line, and wait... hours pass. It's so boring, my gunner is shooting parked cars to see if they'll blow up like the movies. They don't. I start seeing mild hallucinations from the sleep deprivation, and the massive amount of tracers from the VVS-2 only makes it worse. I watch Scooby-Doo and Shaggy walk through my field of view while the cars burn in front of us.

As we're moving to the next phase line, one of the burning cars gas tanks did finally explode, but it was behind us, so I didn't see it.

Next phase line, more waiting, finally time to remove the VVS-2. These things were such pieces of shit, they didn't even latch in properly, so I would strap it in place from the top of the driver's hatch. This thing weighed a good 30-40 lbs, and I'd had it fall out and land on my nuts before. So I crawled out of my hole, unstrapped the VVS-2, crawled back in, and put the regular periscope back in. Daylight, wew.

And then the attack started. Small arms fire from rooftops, so the vehicle commanders have to button up. Usually on Bradleys they would ride with their top half sticking out of the turret.

Then, boom the Bradley in front of me gets rocked by an RPG. Everyone is fine, and now they want all the dismounts out of the Bradleys so that they don't get fucked up. 2nd platoon takes the rooftop of the building to the left of us. I think to myself, "That's not a very bright idea, silhouetting themselves on a rooftop...", then, I watched it happen too fast to even say anything, the streak of another RPG, and boom, there goes the rooftop. The Bradley in front of us is engaging the building the RPGs are flying from, but RPGs are still coming out of it.

Sidenote: my buddy from second platoon told me later that they were going back downstairs from the rooftop and the RPG blew up right behind him, like he didn't even see it coming, and it felt like someone pushed him down the stairs.

So, yeah, this RPG man is like superman or something, he will not fucking die. Then I hear a bigger boom, and I can feel it through my body. There's a huge fucking dust cloud to the left of the building the RPGs are coming from. The dust starts to clear, and it's a fucking Abrams tank shooting at the building. And just like that, another fucking RPG comes flying out at the tank. It ricochets off the tank and blows up beside it. I tell you what, though, watching a tank fire its main gun in combat will get your dick hard.

So, finally they drop a JDAM on the building, and the RPGs stop. The dismounts go and clear the building and the one next to it. They found his body. The dude wasn't even in the building where the RPGs were flying from. He was in the building behind it, firing from that building, through the windows in the building in front of him.

There's more combat that takes place, but it's not what I wanted to get into.

About 3 days into retaking the city, my buddy tells me there's no flyers or pamphlets or anything. It hadn't been particularly windy during that week, so if there had been any, they would still have been in the streets.

We went outside the city to refit, and the Stars and Stripes had a headline like, "80 Insurgents Killed First Day"

We all laughed. There was more like a dozen insurgents..... but there were 80 bodies.

I think we lost one person in the whole brigade in that battle.

But that line, "anyone on the streets is to be considered hostile", still bothers me. They basically lied to us. I mean, yeah, there were people in the city trying to kill us, but there were also plenty of civilians there. There was no warning.

But, then again, if there were soldiers on the battlefield scared to pull the trigger, that could have cost lives on our side.

Edit: also, I was trying to get a combat jerk in, I had my dick out, and was stroking it when the RPG hit the Bradley in front of me. Then it dawned on me, "what will they tell my mother when they pull my lifeless corpse from the driver's hole, dick in hand?"

I put my dick away at that point.

I told my buddies about it a while after, and they all said that I should've kept going, if I had died, they would tell my mother that I died doing what I loved most.
